title: The Bullet Cluster Under EFC: Confronting Entropy-Gradient Gravity with JWST-Era Mass Reconstructions
description: Analytical confrontation of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) with three JWST-era Bullet Cluster mass reconstructions: highest-resolution mass map, spectroscopically anchored lens model, and a revised ~10:1 minor-merger mass ratio. Paper tightens EFC’s structural constraints, registers the A_sig shock-front asymmetry test, reports a null baseline on a PIEMD model, and assesses qualitative consistency of EFC’s regime-transition (mu≈1.1, Sigma≈1.2) with new profiles without introducing new parameters.
author: Morten Magnusson

asig_operator.description: Pre-registered directional lensing residual estimator measuring shock-locked asymmetry across the Chandra shock front after subtracting a density-based mass model.

delta_kappa.description: Definition of convergence residuals used in constructing A_sig.

virial_masses.description: JWST+DECam virial mass measurements (Cho et al. 2025) establishing a ~10:1 minor merger.

sidm_bound.description: Tightened self-interacting dark matter cross-section upper limit from Cha et al. (2025); EFC predicts no dark-matter particle (\sigma/m = 0 by construction).

regime_transition.description: EFC’s qualitative regime-transition expectation at cluster scales: mild gravitational enhancement (mu) and lensing response (Sigma) relative to GR.

key_results.main_finding: JWST-era reconstructions and the confirmed ~10:1 merger tighten EFC’s structural constraints; the pre-registered A_sig pipeline’s PIEMD baseline yields a null (A_sig ≈ −6.9×10^−4, p=0.98), while regime-transition values (mu≈1.1, Sigma≈1.2) show qualitative consistency but remain insufficient alone to explain the full mass discrepancy.

sealed_predictions.statement: At cluster scales, EFC yields a mild regime transition with mu_cluster ≈ 1.1 and Sigma_cluster ≈ 1.2, leading to partial enhancement of gravity/lensing over GR without invoking particle dark matter.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Relativistic EFC solution on the Cho et al. (2025) profiles and JWST mass maps; if the inferred mass discrepancy cannot be reduced without exceeding mu_cluster or Sigma_cluster beyond ~1.2, the prediction fails.

sealed_predictions.statement: Entropy-gradient lensing produces a non-zero A_sig aligned with the Chandra shock front after subtracting a density-only mass model.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Application of the pre-registered A_sig operator to JWST-era reconstructions using the locked geometry and strip parameters; a robust A_sig ≈ 0 result at high significance would falsify the prediction.

kill_criteria: KC1: Using the pre-registered A_sig pipeline (shock_line_x_kpc=480, shock_normal=[-1,0], strip_width=200 kpc, strip_length=400 kpc, 512x512 grid) on JWST-era mass maps (Cha 2025; Rihtaršič 2026), the measured A_sig is consistent with zero at |A_sig| < 0.005 with ≥3σ significance (p ≤ 0.003) across at least two independent reconstructions and bootstrap resamples—this falsifies EFC’s entropy-gradient lensing.

KC2: With all EFC parameters frozen to Ledger v3.11 and no new parameters, a relativistic EFC solution on the Cho et al. (2025) profiles fails to account for the lensing/gas offsets and total mass discrepancy unless mu_cluster or Sigma_cluster exceed 1.25, or requires >10% shifts in frozen parameters (e.g., k from 0.415)—this violates the frozen-parameter claim and kills the cluster-scale EFC regime.

KC3: Future high-precision reconstructions demonstrate that the observed lensing peaks are fully isotropic with respect to the Chandra shock discontinuity (no directional residuals) while maintaining ICL–mass alignment <5 kpc RMS over the subcluster and all three main-cluster subclumps—this contradicts EFC’s component-sensitive, anisotropic response.

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper is EFC's first dedicated cluster-scale empirical confrontation, using three independent JWST-era Bullet Cluster mass reconstructions to tighten structural constraints and register the A_sig shock-front asymmetry pipeline with a PIEMD null baseline. It does not close any Stage-IV kill criterion or theory gap outright — the regime-transition values (mu≈1.1, Sigma≈1.2) show qualitative consistency but explicitly cannot explain the full mass discrepancy alone, and the A_sig test awaits execution on real JWST convergence maps. The paper's main value is defensive: it demonstrates EFC survives the tightest available cluster-scale data without new parameters, locks in pre-registered falsification criteria for entropy-gradient lensing, and converts the revised 10:1 merger ratio into a simplification of the geometric exclusion argument.
graph_insights: This paper is an orphan node in the graph (no related papers found within 1-2 hops), indicating it opens a new cluster-scale validation branch. It should be connected to any future papers on galaxy cluster lensing, ICM thermodynamics, or entropy-gradient field simulations.

The concepts 'PIEMD', 'convergence residuals', and 'shock front' appear for the first time in the EFC graph — these are cluster-specific observables that will become central if/when the A_sig pipeline executes on real data.
No existing validation tests share observables with this paper, confirming it genuinely extends EFC's empirical coverage to a new scale (cluster mergers) rather than re-testing existing predictions.

The paper's frozen-parameter constraint (Ledger v3.11, k=0.415) creates a rigid edge to the BOSS transfer validation (v3.10) and multi-epoch fσ8 test (v3.11) — any future parameter shift at cosmological scales would propagate to the cluster-scale kill criterion KC2, creating a cross-scale consistency web.

tests_added.name: Bullet Cluster 10:1 Merger Geometry Structural Constraint

The asymmetric merger means EFC need only explain the offset for a small subcluster passing through a much more massive main halo, reducing the required gravitational modification amplitude.
tests_added.prediction: EFC structural constraints are more easily satisfied for a minor merger than for a near-equal-mass merger.

tests_added.name: Bullet Cluster SIDM Bound Reinterpretation Under EFC
tests_added.description: Reinterprets the tightened σ/m < 0.5 cm² g⁻¹ SIDM cross-section bound within EFC's no-particle ontology. Since EFC has no collisionless dark matter particles, the bound constrains nothing in EFC; consistency requires that EFC's effective mass reconstruction does not mimic a self-interacting particle signal.
tests_added.prediction: EFC's entropy-gradient mechanism produces mass–gas offsets without requiring any particle cross-section; tightened SIDM bounds are ontologically irrelevant to EFC.

implicit_consequences: The paper establishes that EFC's entropy-gradient lensing is the ONLY pre-registered mechanism capable of producing directional convergence residuals at the Bullet Cluster shock front — ΛCDM predicts isotropic residuals. This makes the A_sig test a genuine one-shot discriminator, not merely a consistency check.

The confirmed 10:1 mass ratio eliminates the strongest version of the Bullet Cluster objection to modified gravity (which assumed near-equal-mass merger requiring large modifications). EFC's modest mu≈1.1 is more plausible for a minor merger, reducing the explanatory burden.

The PIEMD null baseline (A_sig ≈ 0) means any future detection of A_sig ≠ 0 on real convergence maps cannot be attributed to pipeline artifacts — this is a critical methodological lock-in for credibility.

The paper's three kill criteria (A_sig null at 3σ across 2+ reconstructions; frozen parameters violated if mu or Sigma exceed 1.25; full isotropy with ICL alignment) are more stringent than typical modified gravity papers publish. This raises the falsifiability standard and strengthens EFC's epistemic position regardless of outcome.

The regime-transition values (mu≈1.1, Sigma≈1.2) being explicitly flagged as insufficient to explain the full mass discrepancy implicitly demands the full relativistic EFC cluster simulation (EFCLASS Boltzmann solver + non-linear cluster profile) — this feeds directly into theory-efclass-boltzmann-solver gap.
The paper's reinterpretation of SIDM bounds under no-particle ontology implicitly positions EFC to absorb any future SIDM non-detection as a prediction rather than a surprise.
